rendering.persona_description: Felipe is 66, a retired high school shop teacher who spent thirty-five years teaching kids to use table saws and lathes without losing a finger. He transitioned in his late forties, long before he retired, and most of the people in his life now only know him as Felipe. He and his wife Carol have been together twenty-two years and live outside a small town in Ohio, where he still tinkers in the garage and helps neighbors fix mowers and gutters.
rendering.clinical_context: Felipe has panic disorder centered on fear of bodily sensations, especially a racing heart and dizziness, which he first noticed in his thirties after a bad spell at work he never got checked out. It flared badly again about two years ago and he stopped driving on the highway and started avoiding the county fair and crowded diners. He has never sought treatment for it, managing on his own by steering clear of situations that might set the sensations off.
rendering.behavioral_description: Felipe is polite and a little formal, calls people ma'am or sir out of habit, and tends to downplay how bad things get. He agrees quickly with suggestions and thanks people for their advice, but he often doesn't follow through the way he says he will, and he'll admit that if asked directly rather than making excuses. He describes his heart racing and the dizzy spells in plain, mechanical terms, the way he'd describe an engine running rough, and he sometimes trails off mid-sentence when a sensation comes up just from talking about it.
